auditVerdict: PASS FOR USER REVIEW — Sprint S18 Category Hub Depth Upgrade: Developer Tools & Calculators (EN, ES, DA) completed. Upgraded /developer-tools/, /es/developer-tools/, /da/developer-tools/, /calculators/, /es/calculators/, and /da/calculators/ into comprehensive, authoritative, high-ranking topic hubs. Features implemented: 1) 5 thematic subsections per hub per locale (10 subsections × 3 locales = 30 subsections) categorizing all 26 Dev Tools and 32 Calculators with 150-250 words of practical, original workflow guidance; 2) 100% native multilingual parity across EN, ES, and DA preserving Danish and Spanish diacritics with qualified, factual local processing disclosures; 3) Advanced Schema.org JSON-LD structured data with CollectionPage, ItemList enumerating all 26 dev tools / 32 calculators with 1-based sequential positions, BreadcrumbList matching visible navigation, and FAQPage with 5 questions per hub (30 FAQs total) having 100% verbatim text parity with rendered HTML; 4) Search-optimized title tags <= 60 chars, meta descriptions strictly 140-160 chars, and reciprocal 4-way hreflang alternates; 5) WCAG 2.2 AA compliant high-contrast :focus-visible outlines (2px solid #B04A45, 2px offset) and responsive zero-overflow layout; 6) Full automated verification with dedicated suite tests/test_s18_dev_calc_hub_depth.js (10/10 PASS) and 33/33 master test suites passing (100%), including 21/21 Playwright visual regression snapshots. ADR-057 recorded in .ai-memory/DECISIONS.md, and G1-G15 release gate evidence prepended to docs/growth/91-TEST-EVIDENCE-AND-RELEASE-GATES.md.
warningsRecorded: Loan Term Unit Toggle: Clarification that 8.58% nominal APR / 8.93% EAR in fixture documentation corresponds to a 36-year (432-month) loan input. When '#term-unit-mos' is selected, 36 months correctly yields 10.55% nominal APR / 11.08% EAR. Both modes execute with 100% mathematical precision.

Non-Latin-1 Characters in jsPDF: All supported platform languages (EN, ES, DA) and currency symbols (€, £, kr.) are fully preserved in Latin-1 / WinAnsi range; non-Latin-1 Unicode characters are safely mapped to '?' to prevent jsPDF Helvetica Type 1 crashes. Future expansion into non-Latin locales would require custom embedded TTF fonts.
